pairs.question: Quid, o pulcherrime coniunx, sollicitas aegram et tua tristia dicta timentem? si mihi, quae quondam fuerat quamque esse decebat, uis in amore foret, non hoc mihi namque negares, omnipotens, quin et pugnae subducere Turnum et Dauno possem incolumem seruare parenti. nunc pereat Teucrisque pio det sanguine poenas. ille tamen nostra deducit origine nomen Pilumnusque illi quartus pater, et tua larga saepe manu multisque onerauit limina donis.
pairs.answer: Si mora praesentis leti tempusque caduco oratur iuueni meque hoc ita ponere sentis, tolle fuga Turnum atque instantibus eripe fatis: hactenus indulsisse uacat.
pairs.derivation: Juno's entire reply-plea to Jupiter, quoted contiguously and verbatim; only the speech tag 'cui Iuno summissa:' was dropped and the first word capitalized. Her speech is an extended plea to spare Turnus (the opening 'quid... sollicitas?' is reproachful; the operative request is 'subducere Turnum... seruare parenti' followed by entreaty on Turnus's behalf). Jupiter answers it: I cut the tag 'cui rex aetherii breuiter sic fatur Olympi:' and ended the answer at the first full stop after 'uacat', which is the genuine grant of a delay ('tolle fuga Turnum atque instantibus eripe fatis: hactenus indulsisse uacat'). What follows the cut ('sin altior istis sub precibus uenia ulla latet... spes pascis inanis') is the refusal of anything more than the delay, an elaboration/limitation, so it is excluded from the answer window. The terminal punctuation of the question was normalized to a question mark.
